source_uses.fact: Minerals safeguarding seeks to prevent needless sterilisation of mineral resources and requires local policy/context before conclusions on non-mineral development
NPPF requires Mineral Safeguarding Areas and policies while explicitly avoiding a presumption that safeguarded resources will be worked
Adopted London Plan Policy SI7 promotes waste reduction, reuse, recycling and circular-economy principles
Adopted Policy SI8 requires waste capacity planning and net self-sufficiency, including safeguarding existing waste sites
Current GLA waste policy is driven by the London Plan and supports local management, recycling and circular-economy delivery
Current London waste page states strategic zero-waste and recycling ambitions; these are city targets, not parcel performance
ADD2831 approved an April 2026 update of London-level waste arisings using 2024 population data to inform future borough apportionment to 2050
Circular Economy Statement Guidance applies primarily to referable developments and encourages retention, reuse and adaptable design
New-plan evidence identifies evolving waste policy and the need to protect waste-management capacity
The 2026 Draft London Plan remains under consultation and future waste/minerals policy cannot be treated as adopted
Draft 2026 economic chapter includes industrial-land policy; industrial designation does not itself prove waste or mineral use
Draft place-based policies include industrial-land and growth context but remain strategic and non-parcel evidence

examples: A Mineral Safeguarding Area is not a presumption that extraction will occur
A safeguarded waste site cannot be inferred without exact policy-map/site relation
London waste self-sufficiency targets are city-level and do not describe candidate parcel waste capacity
A Circular Economy Statement requirement depends on scheme scale and policy applicability
The 2026 waste-arising model update informs future policy but is not a parcel waste forecast
Industrial land does not automatically mean a parcel is suitable for waste operations
Draft 2026 policies must not override adopted 2021 SI7/SI8 before adoption
No promotion without exact parcel relation to current minerals/waste policy designations and scheme-specific evidence
